fields.topology_type: Point-to-point serial links between nodes and routing switches, interconnected into a SpaceWire network. Packets are forwarded by wormhole routing through routers using path / logical / regional-logical addresses; there is no shared parallel bus.

master_slave_role_summary.description: Source / destination of packets (instrument, processor, mass memory); has one or more link interfaces.
Forwards packets by wormhole routing; has multiple ports plus a configuration port (port 0).
Broadcasts Time-Codes to distribute system time.
Reads / writes remote memory and registers over SpaceWire.

fields.interconnect_role: SpaceWire is a spacecraft-onboard serial network. Links are point-to-point and full-duplex; routers forward packets by wormhole routing using path addressing (port numbers consumed hop by hop), logical addressing (routing-table lookup), and regional-logical addressing, with group adaptive routing for redundancy. Credit-based flow control and Time-Codes operate across the network.

ordering_guarantees.link: Characters are ordered within a link; a packet is delimited by EOP/EEP.
ordering_guarantees.wormhole: A router begins forwarding as soon as the header is decoded; the packet worms through.
ordering_guarantees.credit: Flow is paced by FCT credit so a receiver is not overrun.

fields.memory_vs_peripheral_regions: SpaceWire is not memory-mapped at the link level; packets are addressed by path / logical address, not by a memory address. RMAP (over SpaceWire) provides remote memory / register access; a router's configuration registers are reached through the configuration port (port 0).

device_classification.node: Source / destination of packets; one or more link ports.
device_classification.router: Forwards packets by wormhole routing; configuration port 0.
device_classification.rmap_target: Executes RMAP memory/register accesses, returns reply.
